impact: Customer support records, including identity and wallet details disclosed in chats or calls, may have leaked; number of customers not stated.
date_note: Time as stated in Coinone's notice (around 04:00 on 12 Nov, timezone not specified); notice published 15 Nov.
title: Coinone says attacker breached its support contractor MetaM and customer consultation records may have leaked
summary: Coinone's own notice of 15 November says an external attacker breached the server of customer-support contractor MetaM around 12 November and viewed or leaked consultation records. Listed data that could be involved includes names, contact details, passwords, resident registration numbers, bank accounts and wallet addresses, varying by customer. Coinone says its account, trading and wallet systems show no direct intrusion and gives no count of affected customers.
plain: A Korean crypto exchange says hackers broke into its support contractor and may have taken details customers shared with support staff.
exec: A supplier breach exposed customer identity data at an exchange; expect targeted phishing against its users.
action: Coinone users who shared a password with support should change it everywhere it is reused, and treat unexpected calls or messages asking for codes as scams.

validation.note: Coinone's own notice and NFTevening both read via fetch agent; they agree on the contractor, dates and data types. NFTevening also cites Yonhap, which could not be opened.

review.note: MetaM, about 04:00 12 Nov, 15 Nov notice, data types, no direct intrusion into own systems, no count: checked against Coinone notice and NFTevening
